newsitem.title: UK: Iraqi-backed Kurds urge UN to push food-oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi-backed Kurds urge UN to push food-oil deal.

text.p: An Iraqi-backed Kurdish faction urged the United Nations on Sunday to implement a food-for-oil deal, frozen after Iraq attacked protected Kurdish zones in the north of the country.

The appeal was issued by the Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP), whose forces have now captured two strategic towns held by rivals in the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), sending refugees racing for the Iranian border.
The two sides have been fighting for decades.
A KDP radio statement, echoing a Baghdad plea for U.N. action on the deal as soon as possible, was monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation.

The deal, which won qualified approval by EU (European Union) foreign ministers meeting in Tralee, Ireland, at the weekend, was suspended by the United Nations indefinitely last week after Iraq's military action in support of the KDP.

It would allow Iraq to sell up to $2 billion of oil to pay for badly-needed food and medicine for ordinary Iraqis. Baghdad has not been allowed to export oil since sanctions were imposed in the wake of its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

Last week the United States fired 44 cruise missiles at military targets in southern Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi President Saddam Hussein's intervention on the side of the KDP in seizing the PUK-held northern city of Arbil.
The radio quoted a spokesman for KDP leader Masud Barzani said that Arbil was "under the control of a capable Kurdish security administration" ready to distribute food in the U.N. deal.

Meanwhile in fresh fighting, besieged PUK guerrillas have pleaded for U.S. help after their lines of defence crumbled under an assault by KDP which captured first Degala and then the town of Koi Sanjaq in a matter of hours.
Iraq has denied accusations by PUK leader Jalal Talabani that Baghdad forces attacked the two towns.

The BBC-monitored KDP broadcast said Arbil could provide facilities to conserve and distribute food commodities that would be supplied in exchange for the sale of oil in accordance with U.N. Resolution 986.

"We will do our best to cooperate with the U.N. agencies and to protect and support them so that they can fulfil their duties to distribute food supplies and other commodities. We will ensure the safety of the UN employees and the smooth progress of their work," the statement said.
"We stress that the situation in Arbil is calm and stable. We will do what is necessary to ensure further stability and security in the city.

"Therefore, we appeal to the United Nations and the concerned governments, particularly the EU governments that again called for implementing Resolution 986, as well as the US government, to implement Resolution 986 quickly in order to alleviate the suffering of citizens in Iraqi Kurdistan and in all parts of Iraq," it said.
